title: Ruth Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ruth chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ruth Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ruth Chapter 2.

questions.question: Who was the kinsman of Naomi's husband mentioned in Ruth chapter 2?
options: Boaz
Elimelech
Mahlon
Chilion
questions.correctAnswer: Boaz
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:1 states that the kinsman of Naomi's husband was Boaz.

questions.question: What did Ruth ask Naomi permission to do?
options: Go to the city to buy food
Go to the field to glean ears of corn
Stay at home and rest
Visit her family in Moab
questions.correctAnswer: Go to the field to glean ears of corn
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:2 shows Ruth asking Naomi to let her go to the field to glean ears of corn.

questions.question: In whose field did Ruth happen to glean?
options: Boaz
Elimelech
Naomi
A servant of the vineyard
questions.correctAnswer: Boaz
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:3 states that Ruth gleaned in a part of the field belonging to Boaz.

questions.question: What greeting did Boaz say to the reapers?
options: The LORD be with you
Peace be upon you
Good morning
Blessings on your work
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD be with you
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:4 records Boaz greeting the reapers with 'The LORD be with you.'

questions.question: Who did Boaz ask about the young woman gleaning in the field?
options: His servant over the reapers
Naomi
Ruth herself
The village elder
questions.correctAnswer: His servant over the reapers
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:5 shows Boaz asking his servant who the damsel was.

questions.question: What did the servant say about Ruth's origin?
options: She is a Moabitish damsel from Moab
She is from Bethlehem
She is a local Israelite
She is from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: She is a Moabitish damsel from Moab
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:6 reveals the servant identifying Ruth as the Moabitish damsel who came back from Moab.

questions.question: How long had Ruth been gleaning before she came to the house?
options: From the morning until now
Only a short while
Since midday
After sunset
questions.correctAnswer: From the morning until now
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:7 states she had continued gleaning from morning until that time.

questions.question: What did Boaz instruct Ruth regarding where she should glean?
options: Not to glean in another field but stay close to his maidens
To glean in any field she chooses
To gather only after the reapers leave
To glean near the town market
questions.correctAnswer: Not to glean in another field but stay close to his maidens
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:8 shows Boaz telling Ruth to abide near his maidens and not to go to another field.

questions.question: True or False: Boaz told Ruth that the young men were allowed to touch her while she gleaned.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:9 states Boaz charged the young men not to touch Ruth.

questions.question: True or False: Ruth was a stranger in the land and felt grateful that Boaz took notice of her.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:10 records Ruth expressing gratitude to Boaz for noticing her despite her being a stranger.

questions.question: What had Boaz noticed about Ruth's behavior since her husband's death?
options: Her kindness to Naomi and leaving her own country
Her disobedience to Naomi
Her plans to return to Moab
Her refusal to work in the field
questions.correctAnswer: Her kindness to Naomi and leaving her own country
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:11 explains Boaz acknowledging all Ruth had done for Naomi and leaving her native land.

questions.question: What blessing did Boaz pronounce upon Ruth?
options: The LORD recompense thy work and give a full reward
May you find riches in another land
May you return safely to Moab
May you rest and not work anymore
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD recompense thy work and give a full reward
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:12 contains Boaz's blessing that the LORD would reward Ruth fully for her work.

questions.question: True or False: Boaz invited Ruth to eat with the reapers during mealtime.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:14 shows Boaz inviting Ruth to come eat with the reapers at mealtime.

questions.question: True or False: Boaz commanded his young men to reproach Ruth while she gleaned.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:15 states Boaz ordered his men not to reproach Ruth but to let her glean freely.

questions.question: In Ruth 2, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Boaz tells Ruth to stay near his maidens
Boaz greets the reapers
Ruth asks Naomi to go glean in the field
Boaz commands his young men to leave grain for Ruth
questions.correctAnswer: Ruth asks Naomi to go glean in the field
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:2 shows Ruth asking Naomi to let her glean first, which happens before Boaz's instructions and greetings.

medium.title: Ruth Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ruth Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What specific instruction does Boaz give to Ruth regarding where she should glean in the field?
options: To glean in another field far from his servants
To stay close to his maidens and glean where they reap
To gather only fallen ears of corn in the open field
To glean only from the edges of the field
questions.correctAnswer: To stay close to his maidens and glean where they reap
questions.explanation: Boaz instructs Ruth to not glean in another field but to abide fast by his maidens and keep her eyes on the field where they reap (Ruth 2:8-9). This shows his protective care and provision for her.

questions.question: How does Boaz assure Ruth of her safety among his workers?
options: He tells her to avoid the young men at all costs
He charges the young men not to touch her
He assigns a guard to watch over her
He tells her to glean only at night
questions.correctAnswer: He charges the young men not to touch her
questions.explanation: Boaz assures Ruth by charging his young men that they shall not touch her, demonstrating his protective attitude toward her while she works among them (Ruth 2:9).

questions.question: What reason does Ruth give for finding grace in Boaz's eyes?
options: Because she is wealthy
Because she is a relative
Because she is a stranger
Because she is a skilled worker
questions.correctAnswer: Because she is a stranger
questions.explanation: Ruth humbly acknowledges that she is a stranger and wonders why she has found grace in Boaz's eyes and why he should take notice of her (Ruth 2:10).

questions.question: According to Boaz, what has been fully shown to him about Ruth's character?
options: Her wealth and status
All that she has done for her mother-in-law since her husband's death
Her skills in harvesting
Her knowledge of the land
questions.correctAnswer: All that she has done for her mother-in-law since her husband's death
questions.explanation: Boaz praises Ruth for all that she has done for Naomi since the death of her husband, including leaving her own family and homeland to come to a new people (Ruth 2:11).

questions.question: What blessing does Boaz pronounce upon Ruth for her faith and trust?
options: That she will become wealthy
The LORD will recompense her work and give a full reward
That she will marry a wealthy man
That she will never hunger again
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will recompense her work and give a full reward
questions.explanation: Boaz blesses Ruth by saying the LORD will recompense her work and give her a full reward under whose wings she has come to trust (Ruth 2:12). This reflects God's providential care.

questions.question: How does Ruth respond to Boaz's kindness and friendly speech toward her?
options: She asks to leave immediately
She asks to find favour in his sight despite being unlike his handmaidens
She ignores his words
She offers to work for free
questions.correctAnswer: She asks to find favour in his sight despite being unlike his handmaidens
questions.explanation: Ruth humbly requests to find favour in Boaz's sight because he has comforted her and spoken kindly to her, even though she is not like one of his maidservants (Ruth 2:13).

questions.question: What practical provision does Boaz invite Ruth to share with the reapers at mealtime?
options: To eat bread and dip her morsel in vinegar
To drink wine with them
To have a separate meal prepared for her
To eat only the leftover grain
questions.correctAnswer: To eat bread and dip her morsel in vinegar
questions.explanation: Boaz invites Ruth to come at mealtime to eat bread and dip her morsel in vinegar, demonstrating hospitality and kindness (Ruth 2:14).

questions.question: What special command does Boaz give to his young men concerning Ruth after mealtime?
options: To let her glean even among the sheaves and not to reproach her
To send her away before the harvest ends
To watch her closely and report her actions
To give her all the leftover grain
questions.correctAnswer: To let her glean even among the sheaves and not to reproach her
questions.explanation: Boaz commands his young men to allow Ruth to glean even among the sheaves and to not reproach her, showing respect and generosity (Ruth 2:15).

questions.question: What additional kindness does Boaz instruct his servants to show Ruth while she gleans?
options: To teach her how to glean better
To let fall some handfuls intentionally for her to glean
To provide her with water and bread
To bring her gifts at the end of the day
questions.correctAnswer: To let fall some handfuls intentionally for her to glean
questions.explanation: Boaz tells his young men to purposely drop some handfuls of grain for Ruth to glean and not to rebuke her, showing intentional generosity (Ruth 2:16).

questions.question: How much grain did Ruth gather by the end of the day, and what does this indicate about her labor?
options: About an ephah of barley, showing diligent work
A small handful, indicating limited effort
Enough only to feed herself for a day
None, she was prevented from gleaning
questions.correctAnswer: About an ephah of barley, showing diligent work
questions.explanation: Ruth gleaned until evening and beat out about an ephah of barley, indicating she worked diligently all day (Ruth 2:17).

questions.question: How did Naomi respond upon seeing the amount Ruth had gleaned, and what does this reveal about her feelings?
options: She was displeased and told Ruth to stop
She was pleased and blessed the man who took notice of Ruth
She ignored Ruth's efforts entirely
She asked Ruth to give the grain to others
questions.correctAnswer: She was pleased and blessed the man who took notice of Ruth
questions.explanation: Naomi saw what Ruth had gleaned and blessed the man who had taken knowledge of her, showing gratitude and hope (Ruth 2:18-19).

questions.question: What does Naomi say about Boaz in relation to their family?
options: He is a stranger to them
He is near of kin, one of their next kinsmen
He is the richest man in the land
He is a foreigner
questions.correctAnswer: He is near of kin, one of their next kinsmen
questions.explanation: Naomi explains to Ruth that Boaz is near of kin, one of their next kinsmen, highlighting his family connection and potential role in their lives (Ruth 2:20).

questions.question: Based on Ruth 2:14 and 2:15, what does Boaz's treatment of Ruth teach about Christian generosity and hospitality?
options: That kindness should be shown only to relatives
That generosity includes sharing food and protecting the vulnerable from reproach
That workers should fend for themselves
That hospitality is optional
questions.correctAnswer: That generosity includes sharing food and protecting the vulnerable from reproach
questions.explanation: Boaz invites Ruth to share food with the reapers and commands his men not to reproach her, illustrating practical generosity and hospitality (Ruth 2:14-15).

questions.question: What does Ruth 2:9 promise will happen if Ruth obeys Boaz's instruction to stay close to his maidens and glean where they reap?
options: She will have to work twice as hard
The young men will not touch her and she will have access to water
She will be forced to leave early
She will be isolated and unable to glean enough
questions.correctAnswer: The young men will not touch her and she will have access to water
questions.explanation: Boaz promises that if Ruth stays close to his maidens, the young men will not touch her and she can drink water drawn by them, ensuring safety and provision (Ruth 2:9).

questions.question: True or False: Boaz was unaware of Ruth's loyalty and care toward Naomi before she came to his field.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Boaz clearly states that it has been fully shown to him all that Ruth has done for her mother-in-law since her husband's death (Ruth 2:11), so he was aware of her loyalty.

hard.title: Ruth Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ruth Chapter 2.

questions.question: How much barley did Ruth glean and beat out by evening according to Ruth 2:17?
options: About an ephah
About a homer
About a shekel
About a talent
questions.correctAnswer: About an ephah
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:17 states that she gleaned until evening and beat out about an ephah of barley, a biblical measure of volume used for grain.

questions.question: What did Ruth do after gathering her gleaned barley as described in Ruth 2:18?
options: She gave it to the reapers
She took it into the city and gave some to Naomi
She sold it at the market
She left it in the field
questions.correctAnswer: She took it into the city and gave some to Naomi
questions.explanation: Verse 18 explains that Ruth took up the barley and went into the city where Naomi saw it, and Ruth gave to her what she had reserved after being satisfied.

questions.question: What blessing did Naomi pronounce upon Boaz in Ruth 2:20?
options: Blessed be he who feeds the poor
Blessed be he of the LORD, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead
Blessed be he who owns many fields
Blessed be he who is wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed be he of the LORD, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead
questions.explanation: Naomi acknowledges Boaz's kindness and faithfulness, invoking the LORD's blessing on him for his steadfast mercy.

questions.question: What relationship did Naomi describe Boaz as having to them in Ruth 2:20?
options: A stranger from Bethlehem
A near kinsman, one of our next kinsmen
A servant of Elimelech
A foreigner
questions.correctAnswer: A near kinsman, one of our next kinsmen
questions.explanation: Naomi reveals that Boaz is a close relative, a key detail for the Levirate marriage customs later in the book.

questions.question: What instruction did Boaz give Ruth concerning where she should glean until the harvest was finished, as reported in Ruth 2:21?
options: To glean in other fields
To stay with his young men until all the harvest was ended
To go back to Moab
To glean only at noon
questions.correctAnswer: To stay with his young men until all the harvest was ended
questions.explanation: Ruth recounts that Boaz told her to keep close by his young men, ensuring her safety and provision until the harvest concluded.

questions.question: What was Naomi's advice to Ruth about gleaning in Ruth 2:22?
options: To go gleaning in other fields for variety
To stay with Boaz's maidens so she would not be met in another field
To return to the city and rest
To ask for wages from Boaz
questions.correctAnswer: To stay with Boaz's maidens so she would not be met in another field
questions.explanation: Naomi wisely counseled Ruth to remain close to Boaz's maidens, ensuring protection and favor during the harvest.

questions.question: How long did Ruth glean with Boaz's maidens according to Ruth 2:23?
options: Only one day
Until the end of barley harvest and wheat harvest
Until the feast of Tabernacles
Until the end of the grape harvest
questions.correctAnswer: Until the end of barley harvest and wheat harvest
questions.explanation: Verse 23 states that Ruth continued gleaning through the full duration of both the barley and wheat harvest seasons.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God's provision and protection seen in Ruth 2:12 where Boaz blesses Ruth under whose wings she has come to trust?
options: Psalm 91:4
Genesis 1:1
Isaiah 53:5
John 3:16
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 91:4
questions.explanation: Psalm 91:4 uses the metaphor of God covering one with His feathers and under His wings, paralleling Boaz's blessing in Ruth 2:12 about God’s protection.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'kinsman' in Ruth 2:1, which describes Boaz's relation to Naomi's husband?
options: Goel, meaning 'redeemer' or 'kinsman-redeemer'
Navi, meaning 'prophet'
Malak, meaning 'messenger'
Cohen, meaning 'priest'
questions.correctAnswer: Goel, meaning 'redeemer' or 'kinsman-redeemer'
questions.explanation: Boaz is described as a 'goel'—a close relative who has the duty to redeem or redeem family property, a key cultural role in ancient Israel (Ruth 2:1).

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Ruth 2 to emphasize Ruth's loyalty and Boaz's kindness, especially in the way the narrative returns to their interactions by the end of the chapter?
options: Chiasmus
Metaphor
Simile
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: The chapter frames Ruth's initial gleaning and Boaz's protection with a chiasm, centering the narrative on their mutual kindness and loyalty (e.g., Ruth 2:3-9 and 2:18-23).

questions.question: True or False: According to Ruth 2:15-16, Boaz instructed his young men to deliberately drop grain for Ruth to glean and warned them not to rebuke her.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ruth 2:15-16 explicitly records Boaz commanding his young men to let grain fall purposely for Ruth and to refrain from reproaching her.

questions.question: True or False: Naomi wanted Ruth to glean in other fields besides Boaz's to avoid attention, according to Ruth 2:22.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Naomi encouraged Ruth to stay with Boaz's maidens to avoid being found in other fields, ensuring safety and favor (Ruth 2:22).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God's providential care and kindness seen in Ruth 2:12 where Boaz prays for the LORD to recompense Ruth's work?
options: Matthew 6:26
Romans 8:28
Philippians 4:13
Hebrews 11:1
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:28
questions.explanation: Romans 8:28 speaks of God's providential care and all things working for good, echoing the theme of divine reward and protection as seen in Ruth 2:12.

questions.question: What customary cultural practice in ancient Israel does Boaz's kindness to Ruth in Ruth 2 foreshadow?
options: The institution of the Jubilee year
The role of the kinsman-redeemer and Levirate marriage
The Day of Atonement rituals
The Passover celebration
questions.correctAnswer: The role of the kinsman-redeemer and Levirate marriage
questions.explanation: Boaz's protection and provision for Ruth anticipates his role as her kinsman-redeemer, a culturally mandated relative who marries a widow to preserve the family line.

questions.question: What phrase does Boaz use in Ruth 2:4 when he greets the reapers, reflecting the faith context of the narrative?
options: "The LORD be with you"
"Peace be unto you"
"Good harvest to you"
"Greetings, friends"
questions.correctAnswer: "The LORD be with you"
questions.explanation: Boaz greets the reapers with a blessing invoking the LORD’s presence, showing the faith-based community and God's providence over their work.

theological.title: Ruth Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ruth Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by Boaz's command to his servants not to touch Ruth and to allow her to drink when thirsty?
options: God's justice
God's mercy
God's omniscience
God's omnipotence
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy
questions.explanation: Boaz's care and protection over Ruth reflect God's mercy in providing safety and provision for the vulnerable (Ruth 2:9). This mirrors God's merciful character toward those in need (Psalm 145:9).

questions.question: According to Ruth 2, what theological doctrine is illustrated by Ruth's act of gleaning in Boaz's field while trusting in the LORD's provision?
options: The doctrine of providence
The doctrine of justification
The doctrine of sanctification
The doctrine of election
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of providence
questions.explanation: Ruth's gleaning and the blessings she receives from Boaz demonstrate God's providential care in sustaining His people, a theme seen in Ruth 2:3 and 2:12, highlighting divine provision (Matthew 6:26).

questions.question: What combined teaching about covenant loyalty and faithfulness is conveyed by Boaz's recognition of Ruth's devotion and her departure from her homeland?
options: God rewards faithfulness and covenant loyalty
Faithfulness to family is irrelevant to God
Covenant loyalty is based on ethnic heritage
God's blessings depend on wealth
questions.correctAnswer: God rewards faithfulness and covenant loyalty
questions.explanation: Boaz acknowledges Ruth’s loyalty to Naomi and her faith by leaving her homeland (Ruth 2:11), illustrating that God honors covenant faithfulness and steadfast love (Lamentations 3:22-23).

questions.question: How does the narrative of Ruth gleaning in Boaz’s field (Ruth 2:3-7) foreshadow Christ’s redemptive work in salvation history?
options: Christ as the kinsman-redeemer who provides for the needy
Christ as a prophet who teaches the law
Christ as a priest offering sacrifices
Christ as a judge condemning sinners
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as the kinsman-redeemer who provides for the needy
questions.explanation: Ruth gleaning in Boaz’s field foreshadows Christ’s role as the kinsman-redeemer who provides redemption and sustenance to the marginalized (Ruth 2:3-7; cf. Galatians 4:4-5).

questions.question: What does Naomi's statement about Boaz being 'near of kin' teach about God's provision through human agents in redemptive history?
options: God works through covenant relationships and family ties
God acts only through angels
God’s provision is impersonal and random
God’s provision is limited to kings only
questions.correctAnswer: God works through covenant relationships and family ties
questions.explanation: Naomi identifies Boaz as a kinsman (Ruth 2:20), indicating God's use of covenant family structures to accomplish redemption, demonstrating God's providential orchestration (Genesis 12:3).

questions.question: What synthesis about God's faithfulness and human response is drawn from Ruth 2:12 and Ruth 2:23 concerning Ruth's trust and perseverance?
options: God rewards those who trust Him and persevere in obedience
Human effort alone secures God's favor
God's faithfulness is conditional on ethnicity
Trusting God leads to immediate earthly riches
questions.correctAnswer: God rewards those who trust Him and persevere in obedience
questions.explanation: Ruth trusts under God's wings (Ruth 2:12) and perseveres gleaning until harvest’s end (Ruth 2:23), showing that God faithfully rewards trust and steadfast obedience (Hebrews 11:6).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's justice and kindness is revealed in Naomi's blessing on Boaz for not leaving off kindness to the living and the dead (Ruth 2:20)?
options: God’s justice includes steadfast kindness beyond death
God punishes only the living
Kindness is irrelevant to divine justice
God's justice is only retributive
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice includes steadfast kindness beyond death
questions.explanation: Naomi’s statement reflects the doctrine that God's justice is compassionate and extends even to those who have passed, showing the covenantal kindness of God (Ruth 2:20; Micah 6:8).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Ruth's story is merely a human romance with no theological significance. What does Ruth 2:11-12 actually teach about God's recognition of faith and trust?
options: God recognizes and rewards faith expressed through loyalty and trust
God ignores human faithfulness in favor of ritual
Salvation is based solely on ethnic lineage
God's blessings depend on social status
questions.correctAnswer: God recognizes and rewards faith expressed through loyalty and trust
questions.explanation: Boaz acknowledges Ruth’s faithfulness and trust in God (Ruth 2:11-12), demonstrating that God honors faith and loyalty, countering claims that the story lacks theological depth (Hebrews 11:6).

questions.question: What does Boaz’s invitation to Ruth to eat and dip her morsel in vinegar during mealtime (Ruth 2:14) reveal about God’s provision and fellowship in the community of faith?
options: God’s provision includes communal acceptance and care
God’s provision is exclusively spiritual
God’s provision excludes foreigners
God’s provision is limited to the wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision includes communal acceptance and care
questions.explanation: Boaz’s invitation to Ruth to share food with his workers shows God’s provision as not only material but relational, including acceptance into the community (Ruth 2:14; Acts 2:46).

questions.question: What theological insight about God's protective care is gained by Boaz commanding his young men to not reproach Ruth and to purposely drop grain for her (Ruth 2:15-16)?
options: God actively protects and blesses the vulnerable
God permits the exploitation of the weak
God’s care is passive and indirect
God’s blessings depend on personal strength
questions.correctAnswer: God actively protects and blesses the vulnerable
questions.explanation: Boaz’s protective instructions illustrate God’s active care and blessing for the marginalized (Ruth 2:15-16), emphasizing divine justice and kindness (Psalm 68:5).

questions.question: How does Ruth’s declaration to Naomi about keeping close to Boaz’s young men until harvest ends (Ruth 2:21) reflect the doctrine of sanctification as a process of perseverance?
options: Sanctification involves faithful perseverance in God-ordained circumstances
Sanctification is instantaneous without endurance
Sanctification excludes human cooperation
Sanctification depends on external rituals only
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves faithful perseverance in God-ordained circumstances
questions.explanation: Ruth’s commitment to stay close until harvest ends (Ruth 2:21) models sanctification as ongoing perseverance and obedience in God’s providence (Philippians 2:12-13).

questions.question: What does the fact that Ruth was a Moabitess and yet found favor and blessing in Israelite society (Ruth 2:6-7) teach about God’s inclusive grace?
options: God’s grace extends beyond ethnic boundaries
God’s grace is limited to Israel only
Only Israelites can receive God’s favor
God’s grace depends on social status
questions.correctAnswer: God’s grace extends beyond ethnic boundaries
questions.explanation: Ruth, a Moabitess, was shown favor and welcomed by Boaz (Ruth 2:6-7), illustrating God’s grace as inclusive and extending to Gentiles (Ephesians 2:11-13).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal understanding about human humility and divine favor is drawn from Ruth’s bowing down to Boaz and Boaz’s blessing of her work (Ruth 2:10-12)?
options: Humility before God and man invites divine blessing
Human pride guarantees divine favor
Divine favor is independent of human attitude
Only social status grants divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Humility before God and man invites divine blessing
questions.explanation: Ruth’s humble bowing (Ruth 2:10) and Boaz’s pronouncement of God’s recompense (Ruth 2:12) teach that humility is key to receiving God’s blessing (James 4:6).

questions.question: How does Ruth’s story in chapter 2 demonstrate the theological truth of God's covenant faithfulness despite human dislocation and loss?
options: God remains faithful to His covenant people even in exile and hardship
God abandons His people in foreign lands
God’s covenant is conditional on land possession
Human effort alone secures covenant blessings
questions.correctAnswer: God remains faithful to His covenant people even in exile and hardship
questions.explanation: Ruth’s return from Moab and gleaning in Israel (Ruth 2:2-3) show God’s covenant faithfulness sustaining His people despite displacement, consistent with His promises (Jeremiah 29:11).

questions.question: What does Naomi’s advice for Ruth to stay close to Boaz’s maidens to avoid other fields (Ruth 2:22) signify about God's providential guidance and protection?
options: God providentially guides His people into safe and beneficial circumstances
God leaves His people to random chance
God’s protection is only for the rich
Providence excludes human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially guides His people into safe and beneficial circumstances
questions.explanation: Naomi’s counsel to Ruth (Ruth 2:22) reflects God’s providence directing His people toward safety and blessing (Psalm 23:2-3).
